title: N6OL Powerline QRM Monitor configuration
description: Every setting the monitor understands. Sections map one-to-one onto the [tables] of ~/.buzz/config.toml.

audio.title: Audio input
audio.description: Which sound card the receiver is plugged into, and what it is delivering.

input_device_name.title: Input device
input_device_name.description: The sound card carrying the RF-to-audio converted signal.
input_device_name.x-sample-commented: Whatever the wizard finds on your machine. The value shown names one particular sound card and is only an example.
x-notes: Pick this in the wizard's Audio step rather than typing it: it probes every input, shows a live level bar for each, and writes this for you.
The device is resolved by this name at every startup, never by a stored index, because names survive a reboot and indices do not.

sample_rate.title: Sample rate (Hz)
sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate. Must match what the input device is set to.
x-notes: The band is enforced, not advisory. Below 8000 Hz the 4 kHz the waterfall and the analysis look at is above Nyquist, so there is nothing there to measure. Above 48000 Hz the fixed-size ring buffer holds too little history for the analyzer to acquire the way it was tuned, and a powerline arc has nothing to say up there anyway.
16000 Hz is plenty for this measurement and keeps CPU load low, which matters for a monitor that runs unattended all day.

pulse_rate.title: Pulse rate (pps)
pulse_rate.description: Impulses per second from the mains: twice the grid frequency, since a gap fires on both half-cycles.

x-enum-titles.100: 100 pps - 50 Hz grid (Europe and most elsewhere)

station.title: Station
station.description: Who is measuring, from where, and the calibration that turns audio into dBm.

callsign.title: Callsign
callsign.description: Your amateur radio callsign, used in page titles and plot labels.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone name for CSV timestamps and graph labels, such as America/Los_Angeles.

path.title: Output directory
path.description: Where CSV files, plots, and the index page are written.
path.x-default-from-runtime: The home directory, resolved when the program starts.
x-notes: Recordings default to a 'recordings' folder under this path unless [recording] directory says otherwise.

noise_floor.title: Receiver noise floor (dBm)
noise_floor.description: The baseline for the noise-floor reference line on the daily graph.

noise_min_snr.title: Minimum SNR for a detection (dB)
noise_min_snr.description: How far above the noise floor a reading must sit to count as interference-present in the probability summaries.

audio_rf_conversion_db.title: Audio-to-RF offset (dB)
audio_rf_conversion_db.description: Offset applied to the audio amplitude to approximate RF level at the receiver input.
x-notes: Hardware-specific, and the number every dBm and S-unit reading rests on. Calibrate it with the wizard's Calibration step: adjust RF and AF gain until the reading there matches your own S-meter (S9 = -73 dBm, 6 dB per S-unit).
Set the radio up for measurement first: AGC off, widest filter, SSB, preamp and attenuator off, tuned where the antenna is resonant with the tuner bypassed.

summary_start_date_iso.title: Summary graph start date
summary_start_date_iso.description: ISO 8601 date the all-time probability summary graph starts from.

weather.title: Weather
weather.description: Optional weather data logged alongside each measurement. Arcing tracks humidity and wind, so this is worth having.

source.title: Weather source
source.description: Where weather readings come from, or none to leave those CSV columns blank.

x-enum-titles.cumulusmx: CumulusMX - a weather station on your own network
x-enum-titles.openmeteo: Open-Meteo - free public API, no account needed
x-enum-titles.none: None - leave the weather columns empty

url.title: CumulusMX endpoint
url.description: The JSON endpoint of your CumulusMX installation.
x-notes: Adjust the query string tags to match the fields your station actually publishes.

then.comment: `required` alone would pass: both keys are present, holding null. Open-Meteo needs actual coordinates, so the type has to narrow here too.

server.title: Web publishing
server.description: Optional upload of plots and data to a web server over SCP, so the results can be seen from anywhere. Off by default; the monitor runs local-only.

enabled.title: Publish to a web server
enabled.description: Upload output files after each collection cycle. Everything below is ignored when this is off.

host.title: Server hostname
host.description: Hostname or IP of the web server that hosts the published output.

username.title: SSH username
username.description: The account to log in as on that server.

remote_path.title: Remote path
remote_path.description: Where uploaded files land on the server. Must end with a slash.

key_path.title: SSH private key
key_path.description: The passwordless private key used to authenticate, so uploads work unattended.
key_path.x-default-from-runtime: buzz.pem inside the .buzz folder in your home directory.
x-notes: Generate one with: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.buzz/buzz.pem -N ""
Then append ~/.buzz/buzz.pem.pub to the server account's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and confirm it works before switching uploads on.
On Windows use forward slashes or doubled backslashes: TOML reads a single backslash as the start of an escape sequence.

recording.title: Event recording
recording.description: Optional capture of interference events to .wav, replayable later with --playback and renderable to video with --render.

enabled.title: Arm recording at startup
enabled.description: Start with recording armed. The Record button (or R) toggles it while running, and --enable-recording arms it for one run.
x-notes: A recording starts when the analyzer locks onto the pulse train and ends once the signal has been gone for stop_after_seconds. It opens with whatever audio was already buffered when the lock happened and ends with the silence it waited through, so an event that begins and ends while the monitor is running is captured whole, with a run-up and a run-out around it.

directory.title: Recording directory
directory.description: Where .wav files are written. Empty means a 'recordings' folder under the station output path.
directory.x-sample-commented: A 'recordings' folder under the station output path.
x-notes: This is also where --playback looks when given a bare filename rather than a path.

max_events.title: Events to record
max_events.description: How many of the next events to capture before disarming. 0 records every event until switched off by hand.

rearm_reset_minutes.title: Budget reset (minutes)
rearm_reset_minutes.description: Minutes between refills of that budget, which turns it into a rate rather than a one-off. 1440 gives max_events per day, indefinitely. 0 never re-arms.
x-notes: The cycle runs from when the budget was last reset, not from when it ran out, so it keeps its time of day instead of sliding later by however long each day's events took to arrive. A quiet period does not carry unused events forward.
Switching recording off by hand always cancels the cycle too.

max_seconds.title: Longest recording (seconds)
max_seconds.description: How much of the interference to record, measured from the moment of lock. 0 records the whole event however long it runs.
x-notes: This measures the event, not the file: the run-up the ring buffer was already holding comes free on top, as does the trailer afterwards, so the .wav on disk is always somewhat longer than this.

Any min_lock_seconds spent waiting counts against this, since those seconds are part of the event and are kept - 3 there and 10 here gives ten seconds of event, not thirteen. A min_lock_snr wait is not counted: it is open-ended, and charging it would spend the whole allowance before the file was even opened.
Expect an overrun of up to 200 ms, because the recorder works on a poll rather than watching continuously.
A capped recording does not roll over into a second file: the rest of that event is skipped and the next event starts the next file. The cap always wins over stop_after_seconds.

stop_after_seconds.title: Stop after silence (seconds)
stop_after_seconds.description: Seconds without a lock before a recording is closed. This audio is kept, so it also sets how much trailer every recording ends with.
x-notes: Raise it if a flickering signal is being split across several files; lower it to trim dead air off the end.

min_lock_seconds.title: Minimum lock before recording (seconds)
min_lock_seconds.description: How long the interference must be present before a recording starts. 0 records every lock, however brief.
x-notes: A night of two-second blips otherwise fills the directory with files too short to be worth replaying.

Keep it short - 5 seconds or less. It is paid for out of the lead-in, because the audio that comes from is a sliding window a few seconds long: wait two seconds and every recording opens two seconds later relative to the event.
The value is clamped to the lower of the buffer's length and max_seconds, with a warning saying what was used instead.

min_lock_snr.title: Minimum SNR before recording (dB)
min_lock_snr.description: How loud the interference must be before a recording starts, for keeping barely-audible events off the disk.
x-notes: Recording only. It does not change when the analyzer locks, measures, logs, or draws - that happens at a fixed 6 dB SNR in the code, so any value at or below 6 does nothing at all.
A signal that starts quiet and grows louder is not skipped: recording begins the moment it crosses, so the event is caught even if its opening seconds are not.

Unlike min_lock_seconds this cannot be capped, because its wait depends on the signal rather than the clock. Time spent below the threshold is paid out of the lead-in, and the lead-in runs out. Something in the low teens is a reasonable place to start.

render.title: Video rendering
render.description: Where to find ffmpeg, needed only for --render and the loudness probe that feeds it.

ffmpeg_path.title: ffmpeg location
ffmpeg_path.description: Leave empty to search PATH, which is where a normal install puts it.
x-notes: Set this only when ffmpeg is somewhere PATH does not reach: a Windows build unzipped into a folder, or winget's shim directory in a terminal that has not been restarted since installing.
Either the binary or the folder holding it will do. A copy found on PATH is used in preference to this setting.
A monitor that never renders never looks for ffmpeg, so leaving this empty costs nothing.
